Teams use pgvector because it stores embeddings in the same PostgreSQL database as their existing relational data, so they can join vectors with business records and use familiar tools, transactions, and access controls. It avoids the cost and complexity of running a separate vector database, along with the data synchronization and extra operations that come with it. It also supports cosine, L2, and inner product distance, with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes for fast approximate nearest-neighbor search, which powers AI use cases such as semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
